title: The Restoration of All Things
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The restoration of all things is God’s promised renewal of what sin has broken, fulfilled through Jesus Christ. God will bring His redemptive purpose to completion in His people and creation.
summary: The restoration of all things is God’s promised renewal of what sin has broken, fulfilled through Jesus Christ. God will bring His redemptive purpose to completion in His people and creation.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the One through whom God reconciles and restores all things according to His saving purpose. His return brings the fullness of restoration that His resurrection has already guaranteed.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Sin has broken human beings, relationships, bodies, creation, worship, and communion with God. Scripture does not pretend this brokenness is small.

God’s promise is not merely to help people cope forever with brokenness, but to restore what sin has ruined according to His redemptive purpose in Christ.

This restoration is already begun in salvation, sanctification, and the renewal of God’s people, but it awaits final fullness when Christ returns.

The restoration of all things does not mean every person is saved apart from faith in Christ. It means God’s saving purpose will be completed in His redeemed people and renewed creation.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People who live with pain, trauma, disability, addiction, grief, or loss need more than vague positivity. They need the biblical hope that Christ will restore all things rightly.

This doctrine gives hope without minimizing evil. God can promise restoration because Christ has conquered sin and death and will make all things new.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring your brokenness to Christ with hope. Do not call evil good or pretend pain is small, but trust that God’s final word is restoration. Live now as a witness to the coming renewal by pursuing repentance, healing, justice, mercy, and faithfulness.
